title: A regular principal-prime localization is a DVR
statement: Let H and B be commutative rings with an H-algebra structure on B. Assume H is Noetherian, multiplication by g in H is injective, (g) is prime, and B is the localization of H at the complement of (g). Then B is a domain and a discrete valuation ring, and algebraMap H B g is irreducible. No domain hypothesis on H is required.

source.place: Tags 00IP (Krull intersection) and 00PD (principal maximal ideal DVR criterion); principal-prime localization step of lem-sbc-root-normalization-dvr-comparison

proof.text: B is local and Noetherian by localization. Its maximal ideal is the extension of (g), hence is generated by pi=algebraMap(g). Localization preserves the injectivity of multiplication by g, so pi is regular.

For nonzero b, Krull intersection supplies N with b outside m^N. Induct on N. If b is a unit take exponent zero. Otherwise b=pi*c; c is outside m^(N-1), so induction gives b=pi^n*u with u a unit. If b*c=0 and b is nonzero, regularity of pi^n and invertibility of u force c=0. Thus B is a domain. Regularity and nontriviality give pi nonzero. The principal maximal ideal criterion makes pi irreducible, and the unit-times-power factorization criterion gives the DVR structure.

lean.statement:
theorem regular_principal_prime_dvr
    {H B : Type*} [CommRing H] [CommRing B] [Algebra H B]
    [IsNoetherianRing H] (g : H) (hg : IsSMulRegular H g)
    [hprime : (Ideal.span {g}).IsPrime] [IsLocalization.AtPrime B (Ideal.span {g})] :
    ∃ (hB : IsDomain B), letI := hB
      ∃ (hDvr : IsDiscreteValuationRing B), letI := hDvr
        Irreducible (algebraMap H B g)
